title: Secretary of State of Colorado

context.text: Colorado's Secretary of State certified the 2026 general-election ballot on September 4, 2026; the state's official candidate list shows five Secretary of State candidates: Amanda Gonzalez (Democratic), James Wiley (Republican), Sean Vadney (Libertarian), Amanda Campbell (American Constitution Party) and Celeste Landry (Forward Party).

The seat is open: Jena Griswold is term-limited and is running for Attorney General. Gonzalez won the June 30 Democratic primary with 64.4% over Jessie Danielson; Wiley was unopposed in the Republican primary. Alex Astley defeated Sean Vadney in the June 30 Libertarian primary; Ballotpedia lists Astley among withdrawn candidates, and Vadney appears on the state's general-election candidate list.

candidates.name: Amanda Gonzalez

summary.text: Amanda Gonzalez is the Democratic nominee. She is the elected Clerk and Recorder of Jefferson County, where she oversees elections, vehicle services and public records, and is a former executive director of Colorado Common Cause.

background.text: Attorney and former Executive Director of Colorado Common Cause; her survey response says she authored state laws creating automatic voter registration and strengthening redistricting and election security.
Elected Jefferson County Clerk and Recorder; her campaign describes her as the first Latina and first openly LGBTQ person elected to the post.

priorities.text: Experience running large-scale elections: she says she delivered the county's highest voter turnout while cutting costs.
Protecting and expanding voting rights, including ballot drop boxes, jail-based voting and multilingual ballots.
Keeping elections accessible, secure and transparent.

record.text: Serves as Jefferson County Clerk and Recorder, the county's chief election official; the county's October 2026 election notice lists her office's contact information for ballot questions and replacements.

candidates.researchNotes: Her record items are limited to her current office; specific county election actions were not found on pages that could be loaded.

candidates.name: James Wiley
candidates.ballotNote: Unopposed in the June 30, 2026 Republican primary.

summary.text: James Wiley is the Republican nominee, a political consultant and activist who ran as a Libertarian for Colorado's 3rd Congressional District in 2024 before switching parties. His campaign focuses on changes to election equipment and voting procedures.

background.text: Born in Colorado Springs; holds a graduate degree from Colorado State University Pueblo.
Former executive director of the Libertarian Party of Colorado, and director of Project Thaler and Save Our Suffrage, per his survey response.

priorities.text: Releasing internal Secretary of State files related to the case of Tina Peters, the former Mesa County clerk.
Decertifying electronic voting equipment statewide and requiring hand-counted paper ballots; in his words, "One Day, In Person, Voter ID, Paper Ballots, Hand Count."
Placing Colorado public records on a blockchain ledger.

candidates.name: Sean Vadney
candidates.ballotNote: Lost the June 30, 2026 Libertarian primary to Alex Astley (listed by Ballotpedia as withdrawn); on the state's general-election candidate list.

summary.text: Sean Vadney is the Libertarian nominee. He describes himself as a Denver-suburb native who has been involved in politics for about seven years, and his survey priorities include secure ballots, easy business filing and accessible voting for people with disabilities.

priorities.text: Rigorous checks to prevent fraud while keeping voting straightforward.
Making business formation easy and affordable.
Publishing an Accessible Voting Report and requiring accessibility training for poll workers.

candidates.name: Amanda Campbell

summary.text: Amanda Campbell is the American Constitution Party nominee on the official candidate list. No campaign materials or public statements were found.

candidates.researchNotes: No biography, website or statements found.

summary.text: Celeste Landry is the Forward Party nominee and a volunteer election-policy advocate who says she has lobbied at the state Capitol and at Secretary of State rulemaking hearings. Her key messages are the right to vote, better representation including proportional ranked voting, and election integrity.

priorities.text: Opposing efforts to restrict who can vote, including vacancy-election provisions in House Bills 25-1315 and 25-1319.
Voting methods that allow better representation, including rules for cities adopting proportional ranked voting.
Limiting electronic ballot return to voters who need it, such as those with print disabilities.
